```text
# MkDocs 2.0 Analysis

## (1) Plugin/Theme Breaking Changes

**Plugins**: MkDocs 2.0 "won't have a plugin system" and is "removing plugin support to simplify the codebase." This eliminates Material for MkDocs' extensive plugin ecosystem entirely.

**Themes**: The theming system undergoes a complete rewrite. "Navigation is passed to themes as pre-rendered HTML rather than structured data," making advanced navigation features technically impossible and limiting styling flexibility.

## (2) Timeline

No specific release date exists. The announcement states "a release date has not been announced, so planning around a specific timeline remains difficult," though a pre-release version is available for testing.

## (3) Material for MkDocs Maintainers' Position

The maintainers explicitly reject forking as "impractical" due to ecosystem dependencies. Instead, they developed **Zensical**, described as "a drop-in replacement for MkDocs 1.x." They recommend evaluating options and planning accordingly, offering "hands-on support for migration" through Zensical.

## (4) Specific Plugin Compatibility

The article does not mention static-i18n, llmstxt, or mkdocstrings compatibility specifically. It only references the general incompatibility issue.

## (5) Recommended Action Today

Users should "be aware that future updates to MkDocs 1.x are unlikely" and evaluate their options. Material for MkDocs 9.7.5 limits version ranges to prevent accidental MkDocs 2.0 adoption.
```
</details></tool-use>

幫你拆成兩個層面來看：眼前的 warnings、和 MkDocs 2.0 這個未來風險。

---

## 1. 這些 warnings 要不要管？

| Warning 類型 | 例子 | 嚴重度 | 要修 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mkdocs_llmstxt: Page URI 'X.zh-TW.md' not found` (EN build) | 30+ 條 | 🟡 雜訊 | 可選 |
| `mkdocs_llmstxt: Page URI 'X.md' not found` (zh-TW build) | 30+ 條 | 🟡 雜訊 | 可選 |
| `'index.md' contains a link 'llms.txt'... not found` | 3 條 | 🟢 預期 | 不用 |
| `'reference/npx-skills-metadata.md' contains a link '../../skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json'` | 1 條 | 🔴 真 broken link | **建議修** |
| `'skills/project-knowledge-harness.md' contains an unrecognized relative link '../../backlog/'` 等 | 3 條 | 🟠 跨 docs/ 邊界 | **建議修** |
| `GET /agent-skills/zh-TW/sitemap.xml ... 404` / `302` | dev serve 期間 | 🟢 cosmetic | 不用 |

### 真正該修的 (兩個)

**A. `reference/npx-skills-metadata.md` 的 marketplace.json 連結** — 真的指錯位置：
- 寫的是 `../../skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`
- 實際 `docs/reference/` → 上兩層 = 倉庫根的 `skills/` 還對；但 mkdocs 解析的是 `docs/` 內的相對路徑，所以應該寫 `../skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` 或乾脆用絕對 GitHub URL。

**B. `skills/project-knowledge-harness.md` 指到 `../../backlog/`、`../../pitfalls/`、`../../scripts/`** — 這些都是倉庫根目錄、不在 `docs/` 裡，在 build 出來的網站裡點擊會 404。改成絕對 GitHub URL：
```
https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/backlog/
```

### llmstxt 的雜訊（30+ 條）—— 是 plugin 與 static-i18n 的已知互動問題

mkdocs-llmstxt 不認識 i18n：在 EN build 時看到 `skills/*.md` glob 把 `skills/*.zh-TW.md` 也匹配進來，但那些檔案只在 zh-TW 那輪 build 才存在；反之亦然。**功能不受影響**（`llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` 仍然會被產生），但每次 build 噴 60+ 行雜訊。

兩個處理方向：

1. **直接靜音（最務實）**：llmstxt 沒有原生 i18n 支援，多語站常見做法是只讓它在 default language 跑。可以在 `mkdocs.yml` 把 sections 改成顯式檔名清單（不含 `.zh-TW.md`），或開 issue 給 mkdocs-llmstxt 要 i18n awareness。
2. **接受雜訊**：實際 build artefact 是對的，warning 只在 stderr。如果 CI 沒有 `--strict`，根本不影響 deploy。

我的建議是 **先接受**，等 zh-TW 內容真的穩定（你目前那些 `.zh-TW.md` 還在 git status 為 modified），再來考慮要不要花時間根治。

---

## 2. MkDocs 2.0 的威脅有多大？

**結論：短期不痛，中期需要鎖版本，長期要追 Zensical。**

### 發生什麼事

根據 Material for MkDocs 團隊那篇公告：
- MkDocs 2.0 會 **刪除整個 plugin 系統** —— 所有 plugin（i18n、llmstxt、copy-to-llm、mkdocstrings...）全部停止運作
- 主題系統改寫，nav 從結構化資料降級成預渲染 HTML，所以 Material 的進階導航功能 **技術上做不到**
- 沒有 migration path
- Material 團隊 **拒絕 fork**（依賴生態太大），改開新專案 **Zensical** 當 drop-in replacement
- Material 9.7.5 已經把版本範圍限死，不會意外裝到 2.0
- 2.0 沒有 release date

### 對這個 repo 的具體影響

你的 `pyproject.toml`：
```python
"mkdocs>=1.6",            # ← 沒有上限
"mkdocs-material>=9.5",   # ← 沒有上限（但 Material 自己會擋）
"mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.1",
"mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
"mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2",
```

**目前**：完全沒事。1.x 會繼續運作很久，不會自動消失。

**風險**：等 2.0 釋出那天，`uv sync --extra docs` 在新 lockfile 下可能會把 `mkdocs` 解析到 2.x（因為沒鎖上限），然後所有 plugin 一起爆炸。Material 9.7.5 自己有限制範圍會擋一手，但保險起見不該依賴別人的 pin。

### 建議的 solution

**現在做（5 分鐘）**：在 `pyproject.toml` 加上限：

```python
"mkdocs>=1.6,<2",
"mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10",
```

這樣未來 2.0 釋出也不會影響你的 build。

**中期觀察（半年內）**：
- 追 [Zensical](https://zensical.org/) 的進度——Material 團隊自己的 drop-in replacement，是最有可能無痛遷移的路徑
- 你用的 plugin（i18n、llmstxt、copy-to-llm）會不會被 Zensical 原生支援，目前看來生態才剛起步，沒結論

**長期不需要做**：
- 不用現在遷移到別的框架（Docusaurus/VitePress/Astro Starlight 等）
- MkDocs 1.x 是「成熟到不太需要更新」的狀態，社群 plugin 也都還在維護，這個 stack 用個 2~3 年沒問題

---

 `./docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`

```text
1	# How `npx skills` reads catalog metadata
2	
3	This page captures the verified mechanism behind the grouped install UI
4	of `npx skills@latest add ...`. Everything below was confirmed by reading
5	the actual source of the npm package (`vercel-labs/skills`,
6	[`src/plugin-manifest.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts)
7	and [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts))
8	and the official [Claude Code plugin-marketplaces docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces).
9	
10	## TL;DR for this repo
11	
12	- The grouped picker UI you see when running
13	  `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` is driven by
14	  `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — **inside** the `skills/`
15	  directory, not at the repo root.
16	- Every group header is `kebabToTitle(plugins[].name)`. Skills not listed
17	  under any plugin fall through to the **Other** group.
18	- Edit the manifest by hand; run `make marketplace` (= `bash
19	  scripts/validate-marketplace.sh`) to catch broken paths, duplicates, or
20	  on-disk skills that would silently fall under "Other".
21	- We do **not** ship `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — that's only for
22	  single-plugin repos.
23	
24	## How the CLI resolves the manifest path
25	
26	The user's argument to `npx skills add` is parsed into `repo` + optional
27	`subpath`. For this repo:
28	
29	```
30	npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
31	                       └────────── repo ──────────┘ └sub┘
32	```
33	
34	Inside the CLI ([`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts)):
35	
36	```ts
37	const searchPath = subpath ? join(basePath, subpath) : basePath;
38	// ...
39	const pluginGroupings = await getPluginGroupings(searchPath);
40	```
41	
42	So when the install command **includes** a subpath, the CLI reads the
43	catalog from `<repo>/<subpath>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`.
44	
45	| Invocation | Where the CLI looks for the manifest |
46	|---|---|
47	| `npx skills add anthropics/skills` | `<repo>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
48	| `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` | `<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
49	| `npx skills add foo/bar/some/dir` | `<repo>/some/dir/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
50	
51	This repo uses the second form because the `skills/local/` and
52	`skills/vendor/` trees live under `skills/`, not at the repo root.
53	
54	!!! warning "Common pitfall"
55	    Putting `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` at the repo root and then
56	    invoking the CLI with a subpath silently disables grouping — the
57	    file at the root is never read, and every skill ends up in **Other**.
58	    Match the manifest's location to the install command's subpath.
59	
60	## Manifest shape
61	
62	Reference: official [marketplace manifest schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces).
63	
64	```json
65	{
66	  "name": "<unique-marketplace-id>",
67	  "owner": { "name": "...", "email": "..." },
68	  "metadata": {
69	    "description": "...",
70	    "version": "1.0.0",
71	    "pluginRoot": "./"
72	  },
73	  "plugins": [
74	    {
75	      "name": "<group-name-kebab-case>",
76	      "description": "Short description of the plugin / category",
77	      "category": "<for Claude Code /plugin UI>",
78	      "tags": ["...", "..."],
79	      "source": "./",
80	      "strict": false,
81	      "skills": [
82	        "./relative/path/to/skill-dir",
83	        "./another/skill-dir"
84	      ]
85	    }
86	  ]
87	}
88	```
89	
90	What the `npx skills` picker actually consumes:
91	
92	| Field | Used by `npx skills`? | Used by Claude Code `/plugin` UI? |
93	|---|---|---|
94	| `metadata.pluginRoot` | yes (resolves `source`) | yes |
95	| `plugins[].name` | **yes — drives the group header label** | yes |
96	| `plugins[].source` | yes (must be a string starting with `./`; object/remote sources are skipped) | yes |
97	| `plugins[].skills[]` | yes (must start with `./`) | yes |
98	| `plugins[].description` / `category` / `tags` / `version` / `strict` | **no — pass through** | yes |
99	
100	So `category` and `tags` are essentially free metadata for now: they cost
101	nothing to include in the manifest, and any future native consumer
102	(Claude Code's `/plugin` browser, downstream catalog tooling) can use
103	them without us migrating the file.
104	
105	### What the picker actually shows for a skill row
106	
107	Per [`src/add.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/add.ts)
108	(the `groupMultiselect` call), each skill row is constructed as:
109	
110	```ts
111	{
112	  value: s,
113	  label: getSkillDisplayName(s),        // = s.name (SKILL.md frontmatter)
114	  hint:  s.description.slice(0, 57)+'…' // = SKILL.md description, truncated to 60 chars
115	}
116	```
117	
118	So the **only** thing the user sees per skill is `name` + truncated
119	`description` from that skill's SKILL.md. **Nothing in `marketplace.json`
120	is shown per-skill** — not `plugins[].description`, not `category`, not
121	`tags`, not anything. The plugin's `name` only ever appears as the group
122	header above the skill rows.
123	
124	This means: if you want to annotate / re-label / "tag as deprecated" /
125	override the description for a single skill in the picker, the SKILL.md
126	itself is the only knob. There is no "external annotation" mechanism in
127	the catalog manifest.
128	
129	## Group header rendering — `kebabToTitle`
130	
131	The picker turns each plugin `name` into a header label by splitting on
132	hyphens and titlecasing each token. So:
133	
134	| `plugins[].name` | UI header |
135	|---|---|
136	| `document-skills` | Document Skills |
137	| `claude-api` | Claude Api |
138	| `ml-workflow` | Ml Workflow |
139	| `fullstack-nextjs` | Fullstack Nextjs |
140	| `notebooks` | Notebooks |
141	
142	Pick names that titlecase legibly. `claude-api` → "Claude Api" is the
143	official upstream choice and ships in the user-facing UI of
144	`anthropics/skills`, so awkward casing is a known quirk; do not work
145	around it with weird name fields.
146	
147	## "Other" — the auto-fallback group
148	
149	Any SKILL.md the CLI discovers under the search root that is **not**
150	listed in any `plugins[].skills[]` entry shows up under the **Other**
151	group header. This is how `anthropics/skills`'s `template-skill` ends up
152	under "Other" — it's not listed in their manifest's `plugins[]`.
153	
154	Use this to your advantage: a skill that doesn't fit any category yet
155	can simply be omitted from `marketplace.json` and it will still install,
156	just under "Other". Our `make marketplace` validator emits a warning (not
157	an error) for unlisted on-disk skills so they're easy to notice.
158	
159	## Path resolution rules (gotchas)
160	
161	- `source: "./..."` and `skills[]: "./..."` are **relative to the
162	  marketplace root** (the directory containing `.claude-plugin/`), not
163	  relative to the JSON file itself or the `.claude-plugin/` dir.
164	- The CLI rejects any path that does not start with `./` — `../` and
165	  absolute paths are not allowed (path-traversal protection in
166	  [`isContainedIn`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts)).
167	- `metadata.pluginRoot` (optional) is prepended to every plugin's
168	  `source`. We don't use it; we set `source: "./"` per plugin so each
169	  plugin path resolves directly under the manifest root (`skills/`).
170	
171	## Reserved marketplace `name`s
172	
173	These cannot be used as the `name` field, per official docs:
174	
175	- `claude-code-marketplace`, `claude-code-plugins`,
176	  `claude-plugins-official`
177	- `anthropic-marketplace`, `anthropic-plugins`
178	- `agent-skills`
179	- `knowledge-work-plugins`, `life-sciences`
180	- Any name that impersonates an official marketplace
181	  (e.g. `official-claude-plugins`, `anthropic-tools-v2`)
182	
183	This repo's manifest uses **`daviddwlee84-skills`** — the GitHub repo
184	folder is still allowed to be `agent-skills`; only the `name` field
185	inside the manifest is restricted. The validator script enforces this.
186	
187	## Versioning
188	
189	- If `metadata.version` is **omitted** and the marketplace is hosted in
190	  git, every commit is treated as a new version — users always see
191	  whatever's on `main`. This matches `anthropics/skills`.
192	- If `metadata.version` is **set**, users only see updates when the
193	  number changes (semver-style).
194	
195	We currently set `metadata.version: "1.0.0"` as a baseline. To switch to
196	"every commit is latest" semantics, drop the field.
197	
198	## `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json`
199	
200	| File | Purpose | When to use |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Catalog of multiple plugins / categories | Multi-category collections (this repo, `anthropics/skills`) |
203	| `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | Manifest for a **single** plugin | Single-plugin repos (one bundle of skills, no grouping) |
204	
205	The two files are not redundant. `anthropics/skills` ships only
206	`marketplace.json`; we do the same. A repo can technically ship both,
207	but for a multi-category catalog like this one, `plugin.json` is
208	unnecessary.
209	
210	## Cross-agent portability
211	
212	`npx skills` is a one-way installer: it reads the manifest, then copies
213	SKILL.md files into each target agent's native skills directory
214	(supported targets enumerated in
215	[`src/types.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/types.ts)).
216	Other agents (OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Aider, …) do **not** read
217	`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` natively — they have their own
218	conventions (`.opencode/`, `AGENTS.md`, `.cursor/rules/`, etc.).
219	
220	So the trade-off is:
221	
222	- One `marketplace.json` is enough for cross-agent **install** via
223	  `npx skills add`.
224	- Native discovery in non-Claude agents requires whatever that agent
225	  expects, separate from this manifest.
226	
227	If we ever need a second native catalog format, the cleanest
228	intermediate is to start treating `marketplace.json` as a *generated*
229	artifact from a canonical YAML and add a generator script. We have not
230	done that yet — single-consumer hand-edit is fine.
231	
232	## Hiding / deprecating a skill without deleting it
233	
234	The CLI has a built-in hide mechanism via SKILL.md frontmatter — set
235	`metadata.internal: true` and the skill becomes invisible in the picker
236	while staying in the repo.
237	
238	Per [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts):
239	
240	```ts
241	const isInternal = data.metadata?.internal === true;
242	if (isInternal && !shouldInstallInternalSkills() && !options?.includeInternal) {
243	  return null;
244	}
245	```
246	
247	```yaml
248	---
249	name: my-deprecated-skill
250	description: ...
251	metadata:
252	  internal: true   # <- hides this skill from `npx skills add` picker UI
253	---
254	```
255	
256	What this does:
257	
258	- ✅ Skill stays in the repo, files unchanged.
259	- ✅ Hidden from the interactive picker by default.
260	- ✅ Still installable on direct request: `npx skills add <repo> my-deprecated-skill`
261	  passes `includeInternal: true` so the by-name lookup finds it.
262	- ✅ Power-user override: `INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1 npx skills add ...`
263	  shows internal skills in the picker as well.
264	- ✅ Compatible with discovery elsewhere (Claude Code's auto-discovery,
265	  this repo's docs site) — `metadata.internal` is a `npx skills` convention
266	  only.
267	
268	When marking a skill as internal, also **remove its path from
269	`plugins[].skills[]`** in `marketplace.json` — otherwise you have a dead
270	catalog entry pointing at a hidden skill. The two settings should not
271	coexist for the same skill.
272	
273	### Why not just delete it?
274	
275	Reasons to use `metadata.internal` over deletion:
276	
277	- Keep the docs page reachable (the skill still renders on the docs site).
278	- Preserve `vendor.yaml` history and `last_sync` dates for vendored skills.
279	- Allow opt-in installs by name during a deprecation grace period.
280	- Keep `git log` / `git blame` continuity for future debugging.
281	
282	If you want it gone for good, delete the directory and remove the entry
283	from `marketplace.json` and (for vendored skills) `vendor.yaml`.
284	
285	### Validator coverage (today)
286	
287	`scripts/validate-marketplace.sh` does **not** currently parse SKILL.md
288	frontmatter, so it won't flag the "internal skill listed in
289	`marketplace.json`" mistake. If we hit this in practice, the validator
290	can be extended to:
291	
292	1. Parse each SKILL.md's frontmatter (e.g. via `yq` or python-frontmatter).
293	2. Error if any path listed in `plugins[].skills[]` resolves to a skill with
294	   `metadata.internal: true`.
295	3. Skip the "falls under Other" warning for internal skills (they
296	   wouldn't show up in the picker at all, so the warning is misleading).
297	
298	This is a deferred enhancement — see TODO if/when it becomes worth it.
299	
300	## Working with the manifest in this repo
301	
302	```bash
303	# Validate the manifest (parses, name not reserved, all paths exist,
304	# no duplicates, on-disk skills covered).
305	make marketplace
306	
307	# Or run the script directly with verbose output.
308	bash scripts/validate-marketplace.sh
309	```
310	
311	After adding a new local or vendored skill:
312	
313	1. Place the SKILL.md as usual under `skills/local/<name>/` or
314	   `skills/vendor/<name>/`.
315	2. Open `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and add the new path
316	   (relative to `skills/`) to the appropriate plugin's `skills[]` array,
317	   **or** intentionally leave it out so it falls under "Other".
318	3. Run `make marketplace`. It will warn for unlisted skills and error
319	   for broken paths.
320	
321	## Source references
322	
323	- `npx skills` package source:
324	  [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) on GitHub,
325	  npm package
326	  [`skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skills).
327	- Manifest read logic:
328	  [`src/plugin-manifest.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts).
329	- Subpath + searchPath logic:
330	  [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts).
331	- Picker UI grouping:
332	  [`src/add.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/add.ts)
333	  (search for `groupMultiselect` and `kebabToTitle`).

```text
1	# project-knowledge-harness
2	
3	A lightweight, file-based memory harness that gives any software project
4	three sharply-separated surfaces:
5	
6	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
7	|---|---|---|---|
8	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
9	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
10	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
11	
12	The skill exists to stop two common failure modes: valuable investigation
13	evaporating from chat history, and the graveyard of `IDEAS.md` /
14	`ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` / `LESSONS.md` files that nobody maintains.
15	
16	## When the skill triggers
17	
18	Future-direction signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "nice to
19	have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來".
20	
21	Past-direction signals: "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", scattered
22	"Common issues" sections across `docs/`.
23	
24	Either: "is there a place for X?" where X is metadata about decisions or
25	history rather than current features.
26	
27	## Structure of the skill itself
28	
29	```
30	skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/
31	├── SKILL.md                      # ~170-line entry point; loads on activation
32	├── assets/                       # Copied into target projects
33	│   ├── TODO.md.template
34	│   ├── backlog-README.md.template
35	│   ├── backlog-doc.md.template
36	│   ├── pitfalls-README.md.template
37	│   ├── pitfall-doc.md.template
38	│   ├── agent-guidance.md.template   # Snippet for AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
39	│   └── readme-roadmap.md.template   # Snippet for README.md
40	├── scripts/                      # Executed during setup or by the agent
41	│   ├── init.sh                   # One-shot setup of all of the above
42	│   ├── todo-kanban.sh            # Validator + Markdown / JSON board renderer
43	│   └── promote-todo.sh           # Atomic active → ## Done move + re-validate
44	└── references/                   # Loaded on demand from SKILL.md links
45	    ├── tag-schema.md             # Priority × effort schema and exact syntax
46	    ├── when-to-add-docs.md       # Backlog vs pitfall vs invariant decision rules
47	    ├── anti-patterns.md          # Mistakes to avoid
48	    └── deployment-exclusion.md   # Per-mechanism ignore-rule cheatsheet
49	```
50	
51	`SKILL.md` is intentionally short and points to `references/*.md` so the
52	agent only loads decision detail when it needs it
53	([progressive disclosure](https://agentskills.io/specification#progressive-disclosure)).
54	
55	## How to apply the skill in a fresh repo
56	
57	The default workflow is one command:
58	
59	```sh
60	skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/init.sh \
61	  --target /path/to/project \
62	  --project-name "My Project" \
63	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
64	```
65	
66	This is idempotent — re-running it skips files that already exist and
67	snippets whose sentinel marker is already present. Pass `--force` to
68	overwrite the three template files; snippets are still appended only once.
69	
70	`init.sh` performs:
71	
72	1. Render `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
73	   `assets/*.template`, substituting `<PROJECT NAME>`,
74	   `<DEPLOYMENT MECHANISM>`, `<IGNORE FILE>`.
75	2. Append the agent guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
76	   (auto-detected; override with `--agent-contract`).
77	3. Append the "Roadmap & lessons learned" snippet to `README.md`
78	   (skip with `--readme ""`).
79	4. Run `todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` to confirm the file is
80	   machine-readable.
81	5. Print the deployment-specific lines you should add to your ignore file.
82	
83	`init.sh` deliberately does **not** edit `.gitignore` /
84	`.chezmoiignore.tmpl` / `.dockerignore` — the blast radius is too high
85	for an automated tool. Use the printed cheatsheet as your TODO.
86	
87	## Bundled scripts in detail
88	
89	### `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`
90	
91	Validates the format and renders a kanban-style board.
92	
93	```sh
94	scripts/todo-kanban.sh                    # default: TODO.md, Markdown board
95	scripts/todo-kanban.sh path/to/TODO.md    # explicit file
96	scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only    # exit code only
97	scripts/todo-kanban.sh --json             # machine-readable lane summary
98	```
99	
100	Validation rules:
101	
102	- First non-empty heading must be `# TODO`.
103	- Sections must appear in order: `## P1`, `## P2`, `## P3`, `## P?`,
104	  `## Done`. Additional headings after `## Done` are allowed (e.g., a
105	  `## Notes` or prune log section).
106	- Top-level list items are validated:
107	  - `P1` / `P2` / `P3`: `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
108	  - `P?`:               `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
109	  - `Done`:             `- ✅ [YYYY-MM-DD] [P#/Effort] Title — summary`
110	  Effort is one of `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL`. Active items may end with
111	  `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`.
112	- Anything that is **not** a top-level `- [ ]` / `- ✅` item — prose,
113	  blockquotes, HTML comments, `---` rules, indented sub-bullets — is
114	  ignored and does not count toward lane totals. This lets you write
115	  inline guidance under each section without breaking the validator.
116	- Compatible with macOS system Bash 3.2 (no associative arrays,
117	  no `readarray`).
118	
119	### `scripts/promote-todo.sh`
120	
121	Move an active item from `P1` / `P2` / `P3` / `P?` into `## Done` with
122	the dated `Done` syntax, then re-validate.
123	
124	```sh
125	scripts/promote-todo.sh \
126	  --title "<substring of the item's title>" \
127	  --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
128	```
129	
130	Behaviour:
131	
132	- Substring match against the title field (case-sensitive). Refuses to
133	  run if zero or multiple active items match — refine the substring.
134	- Inserts the new `Done` entry immediately after the `## Done` heading,
135	  using `date -u +%Y-%m-%d` (override with `--date YYYY-MM-DD`).
136	- Looks up the validator next to itself; if validation fails after the
137	  edit, the original file is restored.
138	- Use `--dry-run` to preview the rewritten file without mutating.
139	
140	### `scripts/init.sh`
141	
142	See the workflow above. Notable flags:
143	
144	- `--agent-contract FILE` — override the auto-detected `AGENTS.md` /
145	  `CLAUDE.md` / `.opencode/AGENTS.md` / `.cursorrules` choice.
146	- `--readme ""` — skip the README snippet (useful for repos with their
147	  own conventions).
148	- `--no-validate` — skip the final `todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` pass
149	  (for scripted bootstraps where validation is checked separately).
150	
151	## Reference docs the skill loads on demand
152	
153	- [`references/tag-schema.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/references/tag-schema.md)
154	  (also surfaced as a human-readable page: [Tag schema](../reference/tag-schema.md))
155	- [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/references/when-to-add-docs.md)
156	- [`references/anti-patterns.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/references/anti-patterns.md)
157	- [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/references/deployment-exclusion.md)
158	
159	## How this repo uses the skill on itself
160	
161	The repo's own [`TODO.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/TODO.md),
162	[`backlog/`](../../backlog/) (when populated), [`pitfalls/`](../../pitfalls/)
163	(when populated), and [`scripts/`](../../scripts/) `todo-kanban.sh` /
164	`promote-todo.sh` are a live example of the harness applied to a real
165	project. The [`make kanban`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/Makefile)
166	target wraps the validator/renderer.
167
```

-<!-- Translators: replace this body with the zh-TW translation. Keep the terminology admonition above. -->
+## 給這個 repo 的 TL;DR
+
+- 你跑 `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` 時看到的
+  分組 picker UI 是由 `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` 驅動的 ——
+  **在** `skills/` 目錄**裡面**，不是 repo 根目錄。
+- 每個分組標頭 (group header) 是 `kebabToTitle(plugins[].name)`。
+  沒被列在任何 plugin 底下的 skill 會 fall through 到 **Other** 分組。
+- 用手編輯 manifest；跑 `make marketplace`（= `bash
+  scripts/validate-marketplace.sh`）抓出壞掉的路徑、重複條目、
+  或會被靜默歸到 "Other" 的 on-disk skill。
+- 我們**不**出貨 `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` —— 那只是給單一 plugin
+  repo 用的。
+
+## CLI 怎麼解析 manifest 路徑
+
+使用者給 `npx skills add` 的引數會被解析成 `repo` + 可選的 `subpath`。
+以這個 repo 為例：
+
+```
+npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
+                       └────────── repo ──────────┘ └sub┘
+```
+
+CLI 內部
+([`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts))：
+
+```ts
+const searchPath = subpath ? join(basePath, subpath) : basePath;
+// ...
+const pluginGroupings = await getPluginGroupings(searchPath);
+```
+
+所以當安裝指令**包含** subpath 時，CLI 會從
+`<repo>/<subpath>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` 讀 catalog。
+
+| 調用 | CLI 找 manifest 的位置 |
+|---|---|
+| `npx skills add anthropics/skills` | `<repo>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
+| `npx skills add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` | `<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
+| `npx skills add foo/bar/some/dir` | `<repo>/some/dir/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` |
+
+這個 repo 用第二種形式，因為 `skills/local/` 跟 `skills/vendor/` 樹住在
+`skills/` 底下，不是 repo 根目錄。
+
+!!! warning "常見陷阱 (Common pitfall)"
+    把 `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` 放在 repo 根目錄、
+    然後用帶 subpath 的指令調用 CLI，會靜默地停用分組 ——
+    根目錄的檔案永遠不會被讀，每個 skill 都會落到 **Other**。
+    讓 manifest 的位置匹配安裝指令的 subpath。
+
+## Manifest 形狀
+
+參考：官方
+[marketplace manifest schema](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces)。
+
+```json
+{
+  "name": "<unique-marketplace-id>",
+  "owner": { "name": "...", "email": "..." },
+  "metadata": {
+    "description": "...",
+    "version": "1.0.0",
+    "pluginRoot": "./"
+  },
+  "plugins": [
+    {
+      "name": "<group-name-kebab-case>",
+      "description": "Short description of the plugin / category",
+      "category": "<for Claude Code /plugin UI>",
+      "tags": ["...", "..."],
+      "source": "./",
+      "strict": false,
+      "skills": [
+        "./relative/path/to/skill-dir",
+        "./another/skill-dir"
+      ]
+    }
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+`npx skills` picker 實際上消費的：
+
+| 欄位 | 給 `npx skills` 用？ | 給 Claude Code `/plugin` UI 用？ |
+|---|---|---|
+| `metadata.pluginRoot` | yes (解析 `source`) | yes |
+| `plugins[].name` | **yes — 驅動分組標頭文字** | yes |
+| `plugins[].source` | yes (必須是以 `./` 開頭的字串；object/remote source 會被跳過) | yes |
+| `plugins[].skills[]` | yes (必須以 `./` 開頭) | yes |
+| `plugins[].description` / `category` / `tags` / `version` / `strict` | **no — pass through** | yes |
+
+所以 `category` 跟 `tags` 目前算是免費的 metadata：放進 manifest
+不花成本，未來任何原生消費者（Claude Code 的 `/plugin` 瀏覽器、
+下游 catalog 工具）可以用它們，我們不用搬移檔案。
+
+### picker 對每個 skill 列實際顯示什麼
+
+依
+[`src/add.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/add.ts)
+（`groupMultiselect` 呼叫），每個 skill 列被建構為：
+
+```ts
+{
+  value: s,
+  label: getSkillDisplayName(s),        // = s.name (SKILL.md frontmatter)
+  hint:  s.description.slice(0, 57)+'…' // = SKILL.md description, truncated to 60 chars
+}
+```
+
+所以使用者每個 skill 看到的**只有** SKILL.md 的 `name` + 截斷的
+`description`。**`marketplace.json` 中沒有任何東西會 per-skill 顯示**
+—— 不是 `plugins[].description`，不是 `category`，不是 `tags`，什麼都不是。
+plugin 的 `name` 只會以分組標頭出現在 skill 列上方。
+
+意思是：如果你想對 picker 中單一 skill 加註解 / 改標籤 /「標為棄用」/
+覆寫 description，**SKILL.md 本身是唯一的旋鈕 (knob)**。catalog manifest
+中沒有「外部註解」機制。
+
+## 分組標頭渲染 —— `kebabToTitle`
+
+picker 把每個 plugin `name` 用連字號 (hyphen) 切開、每個 token 做
+titlecase，組成標頭文字。所以：
+
+| `plugins[].name` | UI 標頭 |
+|---|---|
+| `document-skills` | Document Skills |
+| `claude-api` | Claude Api |
+| `ml-workflow` | Ml Workflow |
+| `fullstack-nextjs` | Fullstack Nextjs |
+| `notebooks` | Notebooks |
+
+挑 titlecase 起來能讀的名字。`claude-api` → "Claude Api" 是官方
+upstream 的選擇，現役在 `anthropics/skills` 的使用者介面中出現，
+所以彆扭的 casing 是已知怪癖；不要用奇怪的 name 欄位來繞過。
+
+## "Other" —— 自動 fallback 分組
+
+CLI 在搜尋根目錄底下發現的 SKILL.md，**只要不在**任何
+`plugins[].skills[]` 條目中，都會出現在 **Other** 分組標頭底下。
+這就是為什麼 `anthropics/skills` 的 `template-skill` 落在 "Other"
+—— 因為它沒被列在他們 manifest 的 `plugins[]`。
+
+利用這點：暫時不適合任何分類的 skill，可以單純從 `marketplace.json`
+省略，它仍然會被安裝，只是落在 "Other"。我們的 `make marketplace`
+validator 對沒列出的 on-disk skill 發 warning（不是 error），
+這樣容易注意到。
+
+## 路徑解析規則（陷阱）
+
+- `source: "./..."` 跟 `skills[]: "./..."` 是**相對於 marketplace 根目錄**
+  （含 `.claude-plugin/` 的目錄）的路徑，不是相對於 JSON 檔案本身或
+  `.claude-plugin/` 目錄。
+- CLI 拒絕任何不以 `./` 開頭的路徑 —— `../` 跟絕對路徑都不允許
+  （路徑遍歷保護 (path-traversal protection) 在
+  [`isContainedIn`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts)）。
+- `metadata.pluginRoot`（可選）會被前置 (prepend) 到每個 plugin 的
+  `source`。我們沒用它；我們在每個 plugin 設 `source: "./"`，這樣
+  每個 plugin 路徑直接解析在 manifest 根目錄底下 (`skills/`)。
+
+## 保留的 marketplace `name`
+
+依官方文件，這些不能用作 `name` 欄位：
+
+- `claude-code-marketplace`、`claude-code-plugins`、
+  `claude-plugins-official`
+- `anthropic-marketplace`、`anthropic-plugins`
+- `agent-skills`
+- `knowledge-work-plugins`、`life-sciences`
+- 任何冒充官方 marketplace 的名字
+  （例如 `official-claude-plugins`、`anthropic-tools-v2`）
+
+這個 repo 的 manifest 使用 **`daviddwlee84-skills`** —— GitHub repo
+資料夾仍然可以叫 `agent-skills`；只有 manifest 內的 `name` 欄位被限制。
+validator script 會強制這條。
+
+## Versioning
+
+- 如果 `metadata.version` **省略**且 marketplace 是 git-hosted，
+  每個 commit 都被當成新版本 —— 使用者永遠看到 `main` 上的東西。
+  這跟 `anthropics/skills` 一致。
+- 如果 `metadata.version` **有設**，使用者只在數字改變時看到更新
+  （semver 風格）。
+
+我們目前設 `metadata.version: "1.0.0"` 當作基線。要切到「每個 commit
+都是 latest」的語義，就拿掉這個欄位。
+
+## `marketplace.json` vs `plugin.json`
+
+| 檔案 | 目的 | 何時使用 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | 多個 plugin / 分類的 catalog | 多分類集合（這個 repo、`anthropics/skills`） |
+| `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` | **單一** plugin 的 manifest | 單一 plugin 的 repo（一捆 skill，沒分組） |
+
+兩個檔案不是冗餘的。`anthropics/skills` 只出貨 `marketplace.json`；
+我們做一樣的事。一個 repo 技術上可以兩個都出貨，但對於這種多分類
+catalog 來說，`plugin.json` 是不必要的。
+
+## Cross-agent portability
+
+`npx skills` 是個單向安裝器：它讀 manifest，然後把 SKILL.md 檔案
+複製到每個目標 agent 的原生 skills 目錄（支援的目標列在
+[`src/types.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/types.ts)）。
+其他 agent (OpenCode、Codex、Cursor、Aider、…) **不會**原生讀
+`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` —— 它們有自己的慣例
+(`.opencode/`、`AGENTS.md`、`.cursor/rules/` 等)。
+
+所以取捨是：
+
+- 一個 `marketplace.json` 對於透過 `npx skills add` 做 cross-agent
+  **install** 是夠用的。
+- 在非 Claude agent 中做原生發現需要那個 agent 期望的東西，跟這個
+  manifest 分開。
+
+如果哪天我們需要第二種原生 catalog 格式，最乾淨的中介方案是把
+`marketplace.json` 當成由 canonical YAML **生成 (generated)** 的產物，
+並加一個 generator script。我們還沒這樣做 —— 單一消費者手動編輯目前是 OK 的。
+
+## 不刪除而是隱藏 / 棄用 (deprecate) 一個 skill
+
+CLI 透過 SKILL.md frontmatter 內建一個隱藏機制 —— 設
+`metadata.internal: true`，skill 在 picker 中變不可見，但留在 repo 內。
+
+依 [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts)：
+
+```ts
+const isInternal = data.metadata?.internal === true;
+if (isInternal && !shouldInstallInternalSkills() && !options?.includeInternal) {
+  return null;
+}
+```
+
+```yaml
+---
+name: my-deprecated-skill
+description: ...
+metadata:
+  internal: true   # <- 把這個 skill 從 `npx skills add` picker UI 隱藏
+---
+```
+
+這做的事：
+
+- ✅ Skill 留在 repo，檔案不變。
+- ✅ 預設從互動 picker 隱藏。
+- ✅ 直接請求仍可安裝：`npx skills add <repo> my-deprecated-skill`
+  傳 `includeInternal: true` 所以按名字查找會找到它。
+- ✅ 進階使用者覆寫：`INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1 npx skills add ...`
+  也會把 internal skill 顯示在 picker 中。
+- ✅ 與其他地方的發現相容 (Claude Code 的自動發現、這個 repo 的
+  docs 站) —— `metadata.internal` 只是 `npx skills` 慣例。
+
+把 skill 標為 internal 時，也要**從 `marketplace.json` 的
+`plugins[].skills[]` 移除它的路徑** —— 不然你會有指向一個隱藏 skill
+的死 catalog 條目。同一個 skill 不應該同時有這兩種設定。
+
+### 為什麼不直接刪？
+
+用 `metadata.internal` 而不是刪除的理由：
+
+- 保留 docs 頁面可達 (skill 仍會在 docs 站渲染)。
+- 為 vendored skill 保留 `vendor.yaml` 歷史與 `last_sync` 日期。
+- 在棄用寬限期 (deprecation grace period) 允許按名字 opt-in 安裝。
+- 為未來 debug 保留 `git log` / `git blame` 連續性。
+
+如果你想要永久消失，刪除目錄、從 `marketplace.json` 移除條目、
+（vendored skill 的話）也從 `vendor.yaml` 移除。
+
+### Validator 涵蓋範圍（今日）
+
+`scripts/validate-marketplace.sh` 目前**不**解析 SKILL.md frontmatter，
+所以它不會抓出「internal skill 被列在 `marketplace.json`」這種錯誤。
+如果我們在實務上撞到這個問題，validator 可以擴充成：
+
+1. 解析每個 SKILL.md 的 frontmatter（例如透過 `yq` 或 python-frontmatter）。
+2. 如果 `plugins[].skills[]` 中的任何路徑解析到帶 `metadata.internal: true`
+   的 skill 就 error。
+3. 對 internal skill 跳過「fall under Other」的 warning（它們根本不會
+   在 picker 出現，所以 warning 是誤導的）。
+
+這是個延期的增強 —— 看 TODO，當變得值得做時再說。
+
+## 在這個 repo 裡操作 manifest
+
+```bash
+# 驗證 manifest（解析、name 沒被保留、所有路徑存在、
+# 沒重複、on-disk skill 都有覆蓋）。
+make marketplace
+
+# 或直接跑 script 取得 verbose 輸出。
+bash scripts/validate-marketplace.sh
+```
+
+加入新的 local 或 vendored skill 後：
+
+1. 一如往常把 SKILL.md 放在 `skills/local/<name>/` 或
+   `skills/vendor/<name>/`。
+2. 打開 `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`，把新路徑（相對於
+   `skills/`）加到對應 plugin 的 `skills[]` 陣列中，**或者**故意省略
+   讓它落到 "Other"。
+3. 跑 `make marketplace`。它會對沒列出的 skill 發 warning、對壞掉的
+   路徑發 error。
+
+## 原始碼參考
+
+- `npx skills` package 原始碼：
+  [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) on GitHub，
+  npm package
+  [`skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skills)。
+- Manifest 讀取邏輯：
+  [`src/plugin-manifest.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/plugin-manifest.ts)。
+- Subpath + searchPath 邏輯：
+  [`src/skills.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/skills.ts)。
+- Picker UI 分組：
+  [`src/add.ts`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/blob/main/src/add.ts)
+  （搜尋 `groupMultiselect` 與 `kebabToTitle`）。
+- 官方 Claude Code 文件：
+  [plugin-marketplaces](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces)、
+  [plugins-reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference)。
+- 這個 repo 的參考 manifest：
+  [`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json)。

## MkDocs 2.0 有什麼新 feature？值得 migrate 嗎？

老實說：**目前公開資訊很稀薄，看不出明顯誘因**。我把翻到的東西攤開給你判斷。

### 已知會被「拿掉」的東西

- **整個 plugin 系統會消失**——這是 2.0 最大的設計選擇，目的是「簡化 codebase」
- **theme 系統重寫**——nav 從 structured data 退化成 pre-rendered HTML，所以 Material 那種進階導航功能技術上做不到
- **沒有 migration path**——1.x 專案沒辦法升上去，要重做

### 「新 feature」目前公開的描述

- 官方頁 ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/)) 自我介紹：「a smart, simple, website design tool」——**沒有具體的 feature 列表、沒有 changelog、沒有 migration guide、沒有 release date**
- GitHub discussion #4077 有 26 則回覆討論 v2，但內容主要是社群在抱怨：repo 不公開、缺 license、不接受外部貢獻——**沒有 maintainer 對於「why this design」或「what's better」的具體說明**

### 生態系統的反應

- **Material for MkDocs 團隊明確拒絕跟進**，反而開了 [Zensical](https://zensical.org/) 這個獨立專案，定位是「drop-in replacement for MkDocs 1.x」（注意：是 1.x 的 drop-in，不是 2.0 的 drop-in）
- Zensical 自稱「seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs」、四階段 rollout、有付費分層 (Zensical Spark)
- Zensical 還沒到穩定 release，`compatibility/` 頁也沒明確列出對 i18n / llmstxt 等具體 plugin 的支援

### 我的判斷：值不值得 migrate？

**目前不值得，而且短期內也不會。**

理由：

1. **沒有可感知的好處可衡量**——官方沒有公布 v2 在 rendering 速度、search、UX、template DX 上比 1.x 強的 benchmark 或 demo。連「為什麼移除 plugin」的設計理由都沒講清楚。
2. **Zensical 是更可能的目標**——Material 團隊自己都不打算移到 v2，明顯在 push 你跟著他們去 Zensical。如果你的 stack 重度依賴 Material（這個 repo 就是），未來的遷移路徑大概是 1.x → Zensical，不是 1.x → MkDocs 2.0。
3. **你會失去 plugin 生態**——i18n、llmstxt、copy-to-llm、mkdocstrings 這四樣只要去 v2 就全沒，且沒等價物。對這個 repo 來說 i18n 跟 llmstxt 是核心 feature，去 v2 等於砍腳。

### 建議的觀察姿態

- **6~12 個月後再回來看**：等 Zensical 出穩定 release、列出 i18n / llmstxt 等於支援清單時再評估
- **不要追 MkDocs 2.0 release**——等到生態跟上再說，且最有機會跟上的是 Zensical 而不是 MkDocs 自家
- **Material 9.7.5+ 已經 cap 住 mkdocs<2**，你現在又自己 cap 了一次，雙保險，build 不會被升爆
- 真要早一步嘗鮮，先在另一個小 repo 跑 Zensical 的 alpha，**不要**拿這個 repo 當白老鼠

簡單說：MkDocs 2.0 目前看起來是 maintainer-driven 的「我想簡化 codebase」之舉，不是 user-driven 的「我們要解決什麼痛點」。等真有人能講出對使用者的好處再考慮——而且真到那時候，可能該 migrate 的目標也是 Zensical 不是 MkDocs 2.0。

# Pitfalls format

A `pitfalls/` directory captures non-obvious traps you've already debugged
once, so the next agent (or future you) can grep the symptom and skip
straight to the fix.

This page documents the format used by
[`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md). Same
shape ships in any project that has run the skill's `init.sh`.

## File layout

```
pitfalls/
├── README.md                              # index + cross-reference table
├── <symptom-slug-1>.md                    # one trap per file
├── <symptom-slug-2>.md
└── …
```

The slug is the **symptom**, not the root cause. You search by what you
see in the error, not by the explanation you eventually learned.

## Single pitfall doc — required sections

Each `pitfalls/<slug>.md` should answer four questions in this order:

1. **Symptom** — the verbatim error text or behavior. Copy-paste, don't
   paraphrase. Paraphrasing kills `grep`.
2. **Root cause** — the underlying mechanism, in one or two paragraphs.
```
</details></tool-use>

1	---
2	name: mkdocs-site-bootstrap
3	description: Bootstrap a MkDocs Material documentation site for a repo and (optionally) deploy it to GitHub Pages — including pinned tooling via uv/PEP 723, a GitHub Actions workflow with paths-filter, llmstxt + copy-to-llm plugins so the site is LLM-friendly, and ongoing helper scripts to add new docs pages with auto-nav. Also handles bilingual / multi-language docs (English + zh-TW or others) via mkdocs-static-i18n with a "preserve English originals" terminology rule. Use whenever the user wants to "set up docs", "publish docs to GitHub Pages", "create a documentation site", "add an mkdocs site", "add Traditional Chinese", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual docs", "translate the docs", turn their README/markdown notes into a browsable site, or scaffold the same docs stack as this repo into a new project. Records opt-in/opt-out, stack choice, and language list in `.skills/preferences.yaml` so the agent doesn't re-ask on every session, and respects existing `docs/` content (detect + ask, never auto-migrate). For evaluating skill output quality use skill-creator; for authoring new skills use skill-author.
4	---
5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
26	  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
27	  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7
28	
29	## When NOT to trigger
30	
31	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
32	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
33	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
34	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
35	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
36	
37	## Workflow
38	
39	### 1. Read preferences first
40	
41	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
42	decision:
43	
44	```bash
45	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
46	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
47	```
48	
49	Possible states:
50	
51	| State | Meaning | What to do |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
54	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
55	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
56	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
57	
58	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
59	
60	Ask the user explicitly:
61	
62	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
63	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
64	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
65	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
66	
67	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
68	
69	```bash
70	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
71	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
72	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
73	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
74	```
75	
76	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
77	future invocations.
78	
79	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
80	
81	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
82	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
83	the short version:
84	
85	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
86	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
87	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
88	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
89	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
90	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
91	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
92	
93	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
94	
95	### 4. Scaffold
96	
97	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
98	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
99	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
100	copy-to-llm.
101	
102	```bash
103	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
104	  --site-name "My Project" \
105	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
106	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
107	```
108	
109	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
110	files unless `--force` is passed.
111	
112	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
113	
114	```bash
115	uv sync --extra docs
116	uv run mkdocs build --strict
117	```
118	
119	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
120	
121	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
122	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
123	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
124	Only proceed on explicit yes.
125	
126	```bash
127	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
128	  --repo owner/repo
129	```
130	
131	Flags:
132	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
133	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
134	
135	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
136	in preferences.
137	
138	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
139	
140	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
141	`mkdocs.yml`:
142	
143	```bash
144	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
145	  --section workflows \
146	  --title "My new workflow" \
147	  --slug my-new-workflow
148	```
149	
150	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
151	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
152	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
153	
154	If the project has additional languages configured in
155	`.skills/preferences.yaml` (`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages`), `add-docs-page.sh`
156	also generates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language, with the
157	terminology-rule admonition pre-injected. Use `--lang LANG` to add only the
158	translation for one specific language without re-creating the default.
159	
160	### 7. Optional: add a non-English language
161	
162	The skill supports bilingual / multi-language sites via the
163	`mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (suffix layout: `index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md`).
164	This step is opt-in and decoupled from initial bootstrap.
165	
166	Trigger: user asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "add zh-TW", "i18n",
167	"add Traditional Chinese", "translate the docs", or similar.
168	
169	Read `references/i18n-guide.md` first — it covers the **terminology
170	preservation rule** ("中文 (English original)" format on first mention; no
171	invented translations) which authors must follow on non-English pages.
172	
173	Then run (with `--drop-strict` if your CI uses `mkdocs build --strict` —
174	keeping `llmstxt` will fail strict-mode builds with "Page URI not found"
175	warnings, so the script offers to patch `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and
176	`Makefile` for you):
177	
178	```bash
179	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
180	  --lang zh-TW --drop-strict
181	```
182	
183	This inserts the i18n plugin into `mkdocs.yml`, creates `*.zh-TW.md` stub
184	siblings of every existing page (with the terminology admonition
185	pre-injected), uncomments `mkdocs-static-i18n` in `pyproject.toml`, drops
186	`--strict` from CI/Makefile, and records the choice in
187	`.skills/preferences.yaml`. Idempotent — re-running with the same `--lang`
188	is a no-op.
189	
190	If you'd rather lose `/llms.txt` than `--strict`, use `--remove-llmstxt`
191	instead (and skip `--drop-strict`).
192	
193	After it runs, re-sync deps and rebuild:
194	
195	```bash
196	uv sync --extra docs
197	uv run mkdocs build      # --strict only if you went the --remove-llmstxt route
198	```
199	
200	## Available scripts
201	
202	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
203	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
204	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
205	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
206	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
207	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
208	    `--no-workflow`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
209	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
210	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
211	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
212	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page and insert it into
213	  `mkdocs.yml`'s nav. If multiple languages are configured, also writes
214	  `*.<LANG>.md` stubs for every non-default language.
215	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--lang LANG`
216	    (single-language stub only), `--dry-run`, `--force`.
217	- **`scripts/add-language.sh`** — Retrofit a non-default language into an
218	  existing site. Inserts `plugins.i18n`, creates `*.<LANG>.md` stubs with
219	  the terminology admonition, updates preferences, uncomments the static-i18n
220	  dep. Keeps `mkdocs-llmstxt` by default; auto-patches CI to drop `--strict`
221	  with `--drop-strict`. Idempotent.
222	  - Flags: `--lang LANG` (required), `--name NAME`, `--default-lang LANG`,
223	    `--target-dir DIR`, `--no-stubs`, `--remove-llmstxt`, `--drop-strict`,
224	    `--dry-run`, `--force`.
225	
226	## Reference files
227	
228	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
229	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
230	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
231	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
232	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
233	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
234	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,
235	  pyproject.toml, workflow, linking rules). Useful when the user asks "what
236	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
237	- `references/i18n-guide.md` — Bilingual / multi-language docs setup using
238	  `mkdocs-static-i18n`. Read this **before** running `add-language.sh`. Includes
239	  the verbatim "preserve English originals" terminology rule for zh-TW pages.
240	
241	## Bundled assets
242	
243	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
244	
245	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
246	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
247	  `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`.
248	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
249	  optional-deps group.
250	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
251	  paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy.
252	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
253	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
254	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
255	- `assets/translation-stub.md.template` — Stub used for non-default-language
256	  pages by `add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh`. Contains the verbatim
257	  terminology-rule admonition.
258	- `assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` — Reference YAML block for the
259	  `mkdocs-static-i18n` plugin (used by `references/i18n-guide.md`; the script
260	  builds the equivalent block via `yq`).
261	
262	## Gotchas
263	
264	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
265	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
266	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
267	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
268	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
269	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
270	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
271	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
272	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
273	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
274	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
275	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
276	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
277	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
278	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
279	  Counter-intuitive name.
280	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
281	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
282	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
283	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
284	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
285	- **`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires `theme.language` set to the *default*
286	  language code.** The plugin warns when it's missing. `add-language.sh`
287	  sets it on first run; if you copy pieces by hand, don't forget.
288	- **`docs_structure: suffix` only.** `add-language.sh` writes the suffix
289	  layout (`index.md` + `index.zh-TW.md` siblings); the `i18n_structure: folder`
290	  preference key is reserved but not implemented. Don't paste a `folder`
291	  config into `mkdocs.yml` and expect the script to keep it consistent.
292	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is incompatible with `mkdocs-static-i18n` under
293	  `--strict`.** llmstxt's `sections:` source-path lookups break after
294	  `reconfigure_material` remaps the page index. `add-language.sh` **keeps
295	  llmstxt by default** (most users want `/llms.txt` more than they want
296	  `--strict`'s safety net) and offers `--drop-strict` to auto-patch
297	  `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `Makefile` so the build doesn't fail
298	  on the resulting warnings. Use `--remove-llmstxt` to flip the trade-off
299	  and keep `--strict`. The dep stays in `pyproject.toml` either way.
300	- **`add-language.sh` removes `navigation.instant`** from `theme.features`
301	  because the language switcher's contextual link is incompatible with
302	  instant navigation. Material's plugin emits the warning itself; the script
303	  is just acting on it.
304	- **Don't translate technical terms in zh-TW pages without the English
305	  original.** The terminology rule (kept English in parens on first mention,
306	  no invented translations) is non-negotiable; the stub template injects
307	  the rule as an admonition so authors see it before they start.
308	
309	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
310	
311	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
312	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
313	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
314	have customizations the templates don't know about.
315

# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and why this stack pins `mkdocs<2`

The pinned upper bound on `mkdocs` (and `mkdocs-material<10`) in this skill's
`pyproject.toml.template` is not bit-rot — it is a deliberate guard against
the planned MkDocs 2.0 release. This page captures the situation as of
**2026-04** so future maintainers can decide when to lift the cap.

## TL;DR

- **MkDocs 2.0 will remove the entire plugin system.** Every plugin in this
  stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`, `mkdocs-copy-to-llm`,
  `pymdown-extensions`'s superfences/snippets/tabbed) **stops working**.
- **The Material for MkDocs team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0.** They
  are shipping a separate replacement called **Zensical**, positioned as a
  drop-in for MkDocs 1.x — *not* for 2.0.
- **No release date for MkDocs 2.0 has been announced** as of writing.
  Material 9.7.5+ has internally capped its dependency range to refuse
  MkDocs 2.0 — but we cap explicitly anyway, so a future Material release
  that drops the cap can't silently break us.
- **Don't migrate to MkDocs 2.0.** The realistic future migration target is
  Zensical (or an alternative framework), not 2.0 itself.

## What changes in MkDocs 2.0

Per the Material team's analysis
([blog post, 2026-02-18](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/)):

| Change | Impact on this stack |
|---|---|
| Plugin system removed entirely | `llmstxt`, `static-i18n`, `copy-to-llm` all stop working. No 2.0 equivalents exist. |
| Theme system rewritten — nav passed as pre-rendered HTML, not structured data | Material's advanced navigation features become technically impossible. |
| No migration path from 1.x | A 2.0 upgrade is effectively a rewrite. |
| Closed contribution model | Community can't report bugs or contribute fixes. |
| Currently unlicensed | Unsuitable for production. |

The official MkDocs 2.0 dev docs ([encode.io/mkdocs](https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/))
describe the project as "a smart, simple, website design tool" but **do not
publish a feature changelog, performance benchmark, or migration guide**.
There is no documented user-facing benefit; the design choice is
maintainer-driven (simplify codebase by removing extension points), not
user-driven (solve a specific pain).

## Material team's response — Zensical

[Zensical](https://zensical.org/) is a new project from the Material for
MkDocs team, explicitly positioned as a **drop-in replacement for
MkDocs 1.x**.

What's known:

- "Built by the creators of Material for MkDocs."
- Self-described as "seamless compatibility with Material for MkDocs."
- Has a phased rollout strategy (Zensical's compatibility page mentions
  four phases) and a paid tier called Zensical Spark.
- **Plugin compatibility is unconfirmed** — i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm,
  and similar plugins are not on a published support list as of writing.
- No stable release; not safe to adopt yet.

The fact that Material's own team rejected forking MkDocs ("impractical
due to ecosystem dependencies") and instead built an alternative is the
strongest signal in the ecosystem about MkDocs 2.0's viability.

## Why we cap explicitly

Material 9.7.5+ already constrains its `mkdocs` dependency to refuse 2.0,
which means *today* a downstream `pip install mkdocs-material` won't
accidentally pull MkDocs 2.0. But:

- A future Material release could relax that constraint.
- `pyproject.toml` here lists `mkdocs` as a direct dependency, so
  `uv sync --extra docs` resolves it independently of Material's pin.
- Belt-and-suspenders: pinning ourselves means we don't depend on someone
  else's defensive pin to stay correct.

The cap is `mkdocs>=1.6,<2` and `mkdocs-material>=9.5,<10`. Both upper
bounds use the **next major** as the boundary, not a specific version, so
patch and minor releases of 1.x / 9.x continue to flow.

## When to re-evaluate

Lift the cap (or migrate off MkDocs entirely) **only when all of the
following are true**:

1. A successor framework reaches **stable release** (semver `1.0+`, or
   equivalent project signal of API stability).
2. That successor publishes **i18n support** equivalent to
   `mkdocs-static-i18n` (suffix or folder layout, fallback-to-default,
   per-language search).
3. That successor publishes **LLM-friendly output** equivalent to
   `mkdocs-llmstxt` + `mkdocs-copy-to-llm` (auto-generated `llms.txt` +
   per-page raw-markdown links).
4. The successor's plugin / extension model is documented and not
   maintainer-only-closed (so we can write a new plugin if we need one).

Until criteria 1–3 are met, **the realistic answer is "stay on 1.x."**
MkDocs 1.x and Material 9.x are mature, low-defect codebases; remaining on
them for 2–3 more years is operationally fine.

## What to avoid

- **Don't bump to MkDocs 2.0 to "see what's new."** There's no documented
  changelog and the plugin loss is total, not partial.
- **Don't fork MkDocs 1.x ourselves.** The Material team explicitly
  considered and rejected this; the maintenance burden is too high for
  individual users.
- **Don't adopt Zensical pre-stable.** It's a paid-tier project from a
  small team with no public release timeline; reserve it for a later
  evaluation when criteria 1–3 above are checkable against its docs.
- **Don't remove `mkdocs-static-i18n` or `mkdocs-llmstxt` to "future-proof"
  the stack.** These work fine today and the bilingual + LLM-friendly
  output are core features of this docs stack, not optional polish.

## Re-checking the situation

A periodic review (every ~6 months) is worth doing. Check, in order:

1. [`squidfunk/mkdocs-material` blog](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/)
   — has the Material team announced a Zensical stable date or revised
   their MkDocs 2.0 stance?
2. [Zensical compatibility page](https://zensical.org/compatibility/) —
   does it now list i18n, llmstxt, copy-to-llm as supported?
3. [`mkdocs/mkdocs` discussions](https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions)
   — has the MkDocs 2.0 plugin decision been reversed or clarified? Has a
   release date been set?
4. The dependency caps in this skill's `assets/pyproject.toml.template`
   and the `pyproject.toml` of the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo —
   if the criteria above are met, both should be lifted in the same
   change, with this reference page updated to record the rationale.

## Source links

- Material's MkDocs 2.0 analysis (2026-02-18):
  <https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2026/02/18/mkdocs-2.0/>
- Zensical home: <https://zensical.org/>
- Zensical compatibility: <https://zensical.org/compatibility/>
- MkDocs 2.0 dev docs: <https://www.encode.io/mkdocs/>
- MkDocs 2.0 community discussion (#4077):
  <https://github.com/mkdocs/mkdocs/discussions/4077>

# MkDocs 2.0, Zensical, and the `mkdocs<2` cap

> This page is now maintained as part of the `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` skill.
>
> The full rationale and re-evaluation criteria live in the skill's
> reference file:
> [`skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/mkdocs-2-and-zensical.md)

## Why this exists

This repo's [`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/pyproject.toml)
caps `mkdocs<2` and `mkdocs-material<10`. So does the `pyproject.toml.template`
that `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` writes into downstream projects. That cap is
deliberate, not bit-rot.

In one paragraph: MkDocs 2.0 removes the entire plugin system, so every
plugin in this docs stack (`mkdocs-llmstxt`, `mkdocs-static-i18n`,
`mkdocs-copy-to-llm`) stops working under 2.x. The Material for MkDocs
team has refused to follow MkDocs 2.0 and is shipping a separate
replacement called Zensical, positioned as a drop-in for **1.x**, not 2.0.
Until Zensical reaches stable release with i18n + LLM-friendly output, the
realistic answer is "stay on MkDocs 1.x." The canonical reference linked
above documents the exact re-evaluation criteria.

## See also

- [Downstream docs stack recipe](docs-stack-recipe.md) — full stack
  description (what the cap is protecting).
- [Skill page: mkdocs-site-bootstrap](../skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap.md) —
  the skill that owns the templates and references.
